== Course of events ==

The Queen's grand procession arrived at the garden, a formal sweep of ceremony in the peculiar logic of Wonderland. When it did, Alice—who had spoken boldly to the Queen about the gardeners and had rescued them from the Queen's sentence of execution—chose not to bow.

This refusal stood as a moment of quiet resistance against the Queen's absolute authority. It came in the wake of Alice's escalating encounters with the powerful sovereign: she had answered boldly when interrogated, asserting that the gardeners were none of her business, and had then taken the extraordinary step of rescuing those very gardeners from death by placing them in a flower-pot. Now, as the Queen's grand procession arrived, Alice's choice not to bow seemed to mark a continuation of this pattern of quiet defiance.

What followed made the stakes clear. Alice was compelled to return to the croquet game while the Queen, unrelenting and imperious, continued to order the execution of the other players—a steady continuation of the very pattern of royal command and consequence that had run through every encounter between Alice and the Queen.
